dedupe_keys.name: global map of irrigation areas gmia version 5

description: The Global Map of Irrigation Areas is FAO AQUASTAT's global raster of the area equipped for irrigation around the year 2005, expressed as a percentage of each cell and, in a second grid, in hectares per cell. Further layers give the share of the equipped area actually irrigated and the shares irrigated with groundwater, surface water or non-conventional sources. Version 5 was produced by Siebert, Henrich, Frenken and Burke of the University of Bonn and FAO by combining sub-national irrigation statistics with the location and extent of irrigation schemes, to support global water and food assessments. Coverage is global on a 4320 by 2160 grid of 5 arc-minutes, about ten kilometres at the equator, in geographic coordinates. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): FAO terms: statistical databases fall under the FAO Open Data Licensing Policy and Statistical Databases Terms of Use (licence of this database not named on the pages read). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the actually-irrigated and water-source layers come from survey statistics, so every cell of one statistical unit carries the same value and pixel accuracy is limited; the map describes irrigated area, not canals or other irrigation infrastructure, and has not been updated since version 5. Simulation uses: irrigation water demand and capacity planning in water-resource models, groundwater-dependence analysis and climate adaptation of agriculture. It is part of AQUASTAT alongside the geo-referenced dam database (data-fao-aquastat-georeferenced-dams).
